locations.note: Douaumont: the French assault on the fort on 22 May 1916.
Argonne: trench lines in the forest around the Four-de-Paris, laid out from real trench maps.
Vauquois: a dense trench network around a huge mine crater, modelled on the mine war at Vauquois, Les Éparges and the Haute-Chevauchée.
St. Mihiel: wooded terrain of the salient south of Verdun, fought over in 1915 and again in 1918.
Flanders: muddy, water-filled trenches of the Ypres salient, after Passchendaele, Hooge, Hill 60 and Langemarck.
Artois: a quarry redoubt and slag heaps on the front of the battles of Vimy Ridge, Loos and Neuve Chapelle.
Champagne: a night map of the front between Reims and the Argonne, fought over in 1915 and again in the final offensive of 1918 at Blanc Mont.
Aisne: the early-war map, wooded farmland still little touched by the war where trench warfare on the Western Front began.
Vosges: fighting over rocky, wooded mountain heights.
Picardie: rolling hills between Amiens and Saint-Quentin, after the fighting of 1916 and of March and August 1918.
